A headline dashboard shows C-1's pooled on-time at 0.815 and C-2's at 0.66, which looks decisive for C-1; but that pooling reflects that C-1 mostly ran dense lanes and C-2 mostly ran remote lanes. Under the network's standardized lane mix of 60% dense and 40% remote, estimate the probability that C-2 delivers on time. Round to two decimals.

reasoning_trace.text: The headline pooled figures (C-1 0.815 vs C-2 0.66) are the red herring: they look decisive for C-1 but only reflect that C-1 ran easier (dense) lanes, so they are confounded.
reasoning_trace.label: valid

reasoning_trace.text: The estimate is an intervention: apply C-2 across the standardized lane mix, weighting C-2's within-lane rates by that mix, not by historical assignment.
reasoning_trace.label: valid

reasoning_trace.text: Standard lane mix: P(dense) = 0.60, P(remote) = 0.40.
reasoning_trace.label: valid

reasoning_trace.text: For comparison, C-1 standardized = 0.60*0.85 + 0.40*0.50 = 0.71, so C-2 is actually the better carrier under a common mix, reversing the headline.
reasoning_trace.label: valid

reasoning_trace.text: Requested value: 0.78.
reasoning_trace.label: valid

reasoning_trace.text: Check: C-2 beats C-1 within every lane type, so its standardized rate must exceed C-1's; 0.78 > 0.71 confirms this.
reasoning_trace.label: valid

verification.details: Computed 0.6*0.90 + 0.4*0.60 = 0.78 for C-2 under the standardized 60/40 lane mix (C-1 0.71), showing the pooled headline is a confounded red herring.
